milestone.title: Make config-persistence test hermetic for Linux CI

intent.outcome: andre's CI is green on both Linux and macOS, and the config-persistence test passes deterministically regardless of the host home directory's contents.

problem.description: The integration test `test_add_group_then_save_persists` (andre/tests/config_persistence.rs) browses the real OS home dir to pick a source/target directory during the add-group flow. On the developer's macOS machine it passes (home has subdirs), but in the minimal `rust:latest` Linux CI container `/root` has no subdirectories, so the browse selects nothing, no group is added, and the assertion `groups.len() == groups_before + 1` fails (`1 == 2`). This reds andre's base Woodpecker pipeline on wip/stable and blocks the wip->stable promotion.

in_scope: Add a home_dir injection seam so tests can supply a controlled home (e.g. an optional home parameter on App::new or a test-only override), without changing production resolution behavior.
Update make_test_app / helpers to point the app at a temp home containing a known subdirectory the file browser can select.
Confirm the full suite (cargo test --all --all-features) and clippy stay green.
out_of_scope: Changing production home-directory resolution for real users.
Rewriting other tests that happen to pass today.

design_decisions.choice: App::new keeps real dirs::home_dir; only App::with_home / tests inject temp home
design_decisions.rationale: Satisfies production-unchanged without a manual TUI run; type-safe seam from Q-01.

open_questions.question: Least-invasive seam: a new optional parameter on App::new vs. a test-only cfg/env hook. Prefer whichever keeps the public API clean.
open_questions.answer: Use an explicit optional home_dir parameter on App::new (threaded into AppContext), defaulting to the real system home. Chosen over an env/cfg test hook because env vars are process-global and unsafe under parallel cargo tests; an explicit parameter is type-safe and keeps the public API change minimal and obvious.

work_packages.name: Home-dir injection seam
work_packages.goal: Let callers (tests) supply a controlled home directory to App/AppContext while production home resolution stays unchanged.
work_packages.rollback: Revert the added parameter/threading; the production App::new path is untouched.

work_packages.name: Hermetic test fixture
work_packages.goal: make_test_app points andre at a temp home containing a known subdirectory so the add-group file browser selects deterministically on every platform.
work_packages.rollback: Revert helper changes and remove the temp-home setup.

steps.action: Add an optional home_dir override to App::new (threaded into AppContext), defaulting to the real system home; production behavior unchanged.
steps.tests: cargo test --all --all-features — existing suite passes with the default (real) home; the seam changes no production behavior.
steps.done_when: App::new accepts an optional home dir and the default path still resolves the real system home exactly as before.

steps.action: Update make_test_app/helpers to create a temp home with a known subdirectory and pass it into App::new.
steps.tests: cargo test -p andre --test config_persistence test_add_group_then_save_persists — passes on macOS and in a minimal Linux container (empty /root).
steps.done_when: make_test_app builds the app against a temp home containing at least one selectable subdirectory.

steps.action: Run full suite and clippy locally (make ci or equivalent). CI Woodpecker green is a human follow-up, not a runner gate.
steps.done_when: Local cargo test --all --all-features and clippy -D warnings are green.
